head: Voice chat
title: Memory topics (V01.0.467)
text: Memory topics (V01.0.467): sub-switch Features → Memory check → "Memory topics" (chat.memory_topics) and Me → Conversation → "Memory topics" (mem_topics), both off. In the background (never while someone is talking) the language model in the home network sorts entries without a topic once into a fixed topic: person, home, on the move, work, health, right now, other; any other answer becomes "other", after a failure it tries again only after an hour. Me → Memory then shows the entries in groups; in the detail the person picks another topic (POST /api/profile/memory/{id}/topic), which the model never changes again. The topic is only for display, does not go to the model when answering and changes no rights. Live shows "N ohne Thema", the journal gedaechtnis: themen … gesetzt=N. The quality test has the cases "gedaechtnis-veraltet" (an outdated entry is never stated as a fact) and "gedaechtnis-bestaetigt" (a confirmed one is used).

head: Voice chat
title: Language model settings (V01.0.121)
text: Language model settings (V01.0.121): Under Settings → Language model → Advanced the admin sets the history length (4000–64000 characters, default 24000), web searches per answer (1–3, default 2), the time limit for an answer (60–600 s), top_p and presence_penalty (0 = the server's default) and own keywords that require a tool (one line per tool, e.g. web_search: elfmeter, aufstellung; whole words only, at most 20 per tool, the built-in words always stay). "Restore default" fills in the shipped system prompt, "Show the whole prompt" lists all parts in order and marks the fixed ones. With Features → "Own conversation style" (off) each profile can say under Me → Conversation → Answer, in at most 500 characters, how the assistant should talk to it; the text sits below the system prompt and above the fixed rules, never applies to guests or another voice and cannot be changed with a device key. Fixed: tool rules, handling of outside text, code word, locks and the values of background jobs (learning, briefing, mail sorting, room).

head: Voice chat
title: Roles by voice (V01.0.249)
text: Roles by voice (V01.0.249): With the admin switch Features → Own conversation style → Roles by voice (off) every profile adds up to 8 own roles under Me → Conversation → Answer, one per line like "Butler: polite, dry, with British understatement", and switches on "Roles by voice". "Sei jetzt der Butler", "Wechsle zur Rolle Erklärbär" or "Rolle Butler" switch, "Sei wieder normal" ends the role, "Welche Rollen hast du?" lists them. The panel recognizes these sentences with fixed rules only in the person's own latest message and only for a saved name ("Sei leise" stays a normal question); that answer has no tools, the model only says the result. The active role applies on all devices of the profile, sits in the prompt after the own conversation style and before the fixed tool rules, and changes only the tone, never the rules. Never guests or another voice; roles are changed only in the own browser, not with a device key, and the admin's defaults never hand out roles. Log line: "rolle: set - Butler".

head: Voice chat
title: Wikipedia straight away (V01.0.249)
text: Wikipedia straight away (V01.0.249): With the admin switch Features → Web search → Wikipedia straight away (off, works without a SearXNG address too) and the profile switch Me → Conversation → Answer → "Wikipedia straight away" the assistant gets the tool wikipedia. For knowledge questions ("What is a quasar?", "Who was Ada Lovelace?") the panel fetches the intro of the matching article with one request to the MediaWiki API (at most 1,500 characters, answer at most 1 MB) instead of SearXNG and whole pages; the model reads far less and starts sooner. With no hit on de.wikipedia.org it asks en.wikipedia.org; the admin can enter an own address (then without a second try). Answers are kept in memory for 24 hours (at most 300). The article is outside text: wrapped as data, no switching or saving in the same answer afterwards. "Wikipedia" or "Lexikon" in the question requires the tool; with "only web search and memory" for unclear questions Wikipedia is included. Only the search words leave the Spark. Never guests.

At most 10; without a choice the German and English Wikipedia. The book name is saved without its date (V01.0.261): when the Kiwix replaces a file with a newer one (e.g. …_2025-01 → …_2025-03) the Spark takes the newest automatically; when a book answers 404 it reads the catalog again at once, and "Tell me more" finds the article in the new file. text: Look locally first (V01.0.264): With the admin switch Features → Web search → "Look locally first" (off; time limit 200 to 1500 ms, default 400) and the profile switch Me → Conversation → Answer → "Look locally first" the Spark itself first looks in the own sources for knowledge questions before anything goes out. text: Put into (V01.0.291): Under Me → reMarkable the profile picks which of its own folders new documents go to (default "Spark", created when needed). The Spark only adds new documents there and never changes anything that exists. If the folder is deleted or in the trash later, it takes "Spark" again, says so once and resets the choice.

head: Voice chat
title: Newest first (V01.0.299)
text: Newest first (V01.0.299): sub-switch under "reMarkable notes" (Functions, admin) plus a switch under Me → reMarkable, both off. The Spark keeps when each page last changed (newer reMarkable software names the time per page, else the notebook's; uploaded documents count with their upload). With similar hits the newer passage moves up at most two places, the gain halves every two weeks, a clearly better old hit stays first; this applies to the document search and to "Search locally first". Each hit then carries "changed on …", and the model is told to follow the newer passage where they disagree and say its date. "What did I note last / today / yesterday / this week / last month?" is a fixed rule on the person's own words: the first round must search the documents and gets the pages changed last, newest first; if nothing is in that span, the assistant says so. New notes arrive sooner: between comparisons the Spark looks every 3 minutes with one small request whether anything changed in the account, and only then compares at once (journal "remarkable: account changed, comparing now"). Since V01.0.369 the Spark's own writes (answers, guide, inbox) do not count as a change; when the reM

head: Voice chat
title: More with the reMarkable (V01.0.344)
text: More with the reMarkable (V01.0.344): admin sub-switch "More with the reMarkable" below "Sending to the reMarkable", plus one switch per function under Me → reMarkable, all off (code: app/panel/rmplus.py). *Morning sheet:* at the chosen time (default 06:30, two hours' window) the daily briefing as a PDF with lines for notes. *@Spark:* "@Spark" and a question on a page that is read; after the comparison (for handwriting after reading) "Antwort: …" lies next to it, from the own documents and, if there is one, the web search; each question only once. *Tasks:* lines with ☐, [ ], "TODO" or "Aufgabe:" show up under Me → reMarkable, a reminder only after clicking "Remind". *Meetings:* notebook or first line with "Besprechung", "Meeting", "Protokoll" …: 30 minutes after the last change a summary with decisions and tasks as a new document plus a note. *Week in review:* on Fridays from 5 pm a PDF with the week's main points. *Web pages and attachments:* tools remarkable_page (a public page as EPUB) and remarkable_attachment (the newest PDF or EPUB attached to a fitting mail of the last 30 days, whole files up to 30 MB only), only when the person's own words name an address or an attachment.

head: Voice chat
title: More with the reMarkable (V01.0.344)
text: *Daily inbox:* dictated notes gather in one document "Eingang DD.MM.YYYY". *Spark guide:* an e-book only about the reMarkable functions and the service (comparison, privacy, limits, disconnecting), each function marked on/off; the Spark compares the text every 10 minutes and renews the same document as soon as it changes (a new function, a switch, the admin's permission). A self-test demands a section for every function below "reMarkable notes", so the guide cannot go stale. Only the guide and the day's inbox belong to the Spark and are renewed (your marks in them stay); everything else is always a new document. At most 30 documents of its own a day; never while someone is talking. Notes only go to the language model as data, without tools.

head: Voice chat
title: Answer onto the reMarkable (V01.0.279)
text: Answer onto the reMarkable (V01.0.279): "Summarize the political situation and put it on my reMarkable" puts the whole answer as a new document into the folder "Spark". A fixed rule on the question's own words decides this (put, send, save … plus "on/to my reMarkable", no colon), not the language model: the model only writes the answer, then the panel sends it and says "The answer is now on your reMarkable …" (or why not). This also works after a web search, after which the tool remarkable_note is locked; the destination is fixed, outside text can only shape the content of the answer, never where it goes. Same switches and daily limit as above, only in the own browser or at a speaker with the recognised voice, never guests. Logs → Requests shows "remarkable (Panel)".

text: Targeted tool choice (V01.0.202): a "switch" in the panel (intent.py) sorts every question by fixed rules into a group: smart home, calendar, mail, web search, reminder, list, weather, transit, parcel, contact, memory, document, message, agent, iPhone, small talk or "unclear". It reads only the person's own latest message, never outside text or model output, and writes one weiche: line per question to the journal (intent, the word that matched, number of tools, required tool, lock); the diagnosis filter "Chat" shows it. With the admin switch Features → "Gezielte Werkzeugwahl" and the profile switch Me → Conversation (both off, never guests) the model sees only the tools of a clear question's group (plus "remember"); a group with one tool (weather, web search, transit) makes the first round call exactly that one. The switch only takes away what the rights check before it allowed, never more. After an answer from the web, calendar, a document or a picture, a new request in the person's own words lifts the lock and the old answer is no longer sent along; if the request points at it ("Setz das auf die Liste", "Erinner mich daran", "Und …"), everything stays locked. head: Voice chat
title: The face at the bottom right everywhere (V01.0.359)
text: The face at the bottom right everywhere (V01.0.359): the face at the bottom right is there for every login (not for guests) on every page, over Me and in the phone view, also without the Spark help. One tap starts listening and opens its window with "Open conversation", "Stop" and a field to type in; a second tap stops listening, the second tap of a double tap does not count and marks no text. With the keyboard: tab to the face, then Enter or Space. The page you are on only goes along with "Ask Spark on every page". The wall monitor (/live) stays a pure display without a face.

head: Voice chat
title: Suggesting functions (V01.0.380, off by default)
text: Suggesting functions (V01.0.380, off by default): the assistant points out a function that is still off when it would help, and helps setting it up. Whether a hint comes is decided by fixed rules in the panel (tipps.py), never by the model: (1) a wish without its tool: the switch recognises a group (calendar, weather, shopping list …) whose function is off for you or on the Spark; (2) half set up: e.g. the iPhone app paired but no notifications, a mailbox connected but "Important mail" off, the second sign-in step on but no passkey, an own speaker but no voice taught; (3) repetition: e.g. five web searches in seven days without "Look locally first" (only the kind of question per day is counted, never the words); (4) new for you: the admin switched something on that you never had on. Setting up (5): if it is only your own switch, the face's window shows the "Apply" card (the same rules and checks as "Suggesting settings", ten minutes "Undo"); if it needs details, it shows the steps from the guide (for a profile without the admin's steps) and opens the right Me page, passwords only into the form; "Check" asks the panel whether it works now. If it is off on the Spark, "Ask the admin"

head: Voice chat
title: Lean list for unclear questions (V01.0.220)
text: Lean list for unclear questions (V01.0.220): under Features → Targeted tool choice → "Fragen, die keine Regel erkennt" there is, next to "all tools" (default) and "the language model sorts it", the choice "only web search and memory" (chat.route_model: lean). When no rule recognizes the question and it requires no tool, the model then sees only web_search, history_search and memory_save (as far as they are offered anyway). The request gets about half as long (on tars 2500 instead of 6000 tokens) and the first word comes about a second earlier. A question a rule recognizes keeps its group. Only together with the profile switch, never for guests.

head: Voice chat
title: Classification with probabilities (V01.0.340, `systemone.py`)
text: Classification with probabilities (V01.0.340, systemone.py): dgx-spark-qwen38 v1.15 and later answers fixed questions with probabilities instead of text at POST /v1/systemone (choice, score, yes/no; model name jev-latest, served by the Qwen3.8 lane that already runs, one token per question, no memory of its own, nothing leaves the machine). The panel asks only its own fixed questions and options; the text being judged (the person's own message, sender and subject of a mail, the mail text when tidying, a test answer) goes only into "state", cut to 4000 characters, without control characters, fenced by qwen38 with a random token. The panel decides with fixed thresholds. Only the stored address and key from Settings → Language model, no redirects, at most 64 KB back; an answer naming an option not offered or a value outside 0 to 1 counts as none. When qwen38 is busy (529), too old (404) or too slow, everything goes on as without it. Switches (all off, never guests): Features → Conversation → "Einordnung mit Wahrscheinlichkeit" (chat.systemone, with a "Check classification" button) and Me → Conversation → "Classification with probabilities" (systemone_on). head: Voice chat
title: First sentence sooner (V01.0.220)
text: First sentence sooner (V01.0.220): a long first sentence goes to speech output at its last comma from 50 characters on (before: 120), if that comma comes after at least 20 characters, so the first sound comes earlier.

head: Voice chat
title: Formatted answers (V01.0.451)
text: Formatted answers (V01.0.451): The panel's chat (browser, phone view, Android app) shows Markdown in answers formatted: headings, bold, *italic*, numbered and plain lists, quotes, code, code blocks, tables and links, already while the answer comes in. Built safely (md.js): model text never becomes HTML, every element is made with createElement/textContent, only a fixed list of elements, pictures are not loaded (only linked), links only for http(s) to public addresses (no localhost, no home network, no name:password@ addresses, otherwise the address stays text); they open in a new tab without referrer and name the host when the link text says something else; very long answers (over 60,000 characters) stay plain text. The signs are never spoken: both speech services take the Markdown signs out before every sentence (textnorm.speech_markdown, whatever the switch "do not read out emojis, code and Markdown" says), code is spoken as a word in quotes, links only by their text, code blocks not at all. This runs before the rule "never say passwords", so "Password is …" is not said either. Where nothing can be formatted, clean text without asterisks arrives (textnorm.plain_markdown): Telegra

head: Voice chat
title: Formatted answers (V01.0.451)
text: m, Siri, companion, reMarkable, watch and the speakers' display; the stored history keeps the original. The iPhone app shows bold, italic, code and links (http(s) only) right in the bubble; copy and share give the text without signs. So that the model structures longer answers, only the panel's chat gets the fixed hint chat.WEB_HINT (for spoken answers without tables and code blocks, with "read answers aloud" off with both); short answers stay whole sentences. Checked answers (answer check) now keep their line breaks. No switch: display only, nothing leaves the house. Test: test_markdown.

head: The panel
title: The panel
text: On the first admin login a setup wizard walks through password, language model (with a connection test), voice (to listen to), profiles, access and features, and ends with the live check. Start it again: *Status → Checks → Run setup again*.

head: The panel
title: The panel
text: The menu (since V01.0.145, design "Klar") is a sidebar on the left on computers and a bar at the bottom on phones (Assistant, Me, Status, Manage). At the very top Search (Ctrl K or ⌘ K, since V01.0.265) finds pages, switches, settings, Me, checks, logs and guides; a hit opens the place and marks it. A way in a hint or an answer like "Settings → Spark → Operation" or "Me → Documents" is a link that jumps right there (since V01.0.435). Below are Assistant and Me for yourself, then under *Manage Spark* the admin pages Status, Features (with *Guides*), People and devices (with *Apps and interfaces*) and Settings (since V01.0.265; "Integrate" is gone). Status, Features and People and devices have sub-pages; a number next to "Settings" counts unsaved pages. On a computer "Me" opens as a page right of the sidebar since V01.0.147 instead of a window; another menu entry closes it.

head: The panel
title: The panel
text: - Assistent (assistant): voice chat with the dgx-spark-qwen38 LLM. Speak (or type); the answer comes back as text and streamed speech, sentence by sentence while the LLM is still writing. Hands-free mode listens again after each answer; the space bar or "Speak" interrupts. If nobody says anything for 8 seconds after an answer, the microphone goes off and the status line says so ("Heard nothing, microphone off"); only "Hey Spark" listens all the time. Follow-up without wake word (admin: Features → Follow-up without wake word, off by default; profile: Me → Conversation, off/4/6/8/10 seconds): after answering a spoken question (via "Hey Spark" or "Speak") the microphone stays open for the chosen time, so "And tomorrow?" works without the wake word; if nothing comes it goes off and "Hey Spark" keeps listening. Unlike hands-free only briefly and only after spoken questions; never after typed questions, never for guests, never in room mode. The ESP32 speakers do not have it (they listen for "Jarvis" on the chip). On an iPhone, iOS ends the microphone when the screen locks, the page goes to the background, a call comes in or Siri speaks. The panel notices, says so, gets a fresh microphone

Now the panel measures for every recording at /api/test/asr (app, browser, guests) how long it is clearly louder than the quietest part of the room, in 30 ms pieces (three times the 20th percentile, at least about −46 dBFS, at most −30 dBFS). A lone short word ("Ja", "Okay", "Danke", "Hm") counts only with at least 0.2 s of voice; a spoken "Ja" is longer, so a real yes still goes through. head: The panel
title: History on every device
text: History on every device (since V01.0.457): a profile's conversations live on the Spark. The panel, the Android app and the iPhone app send only the new messages after each answer, and the Spark appends them. When two devices ask in the same conversation (for example today's conversation on the computer and on the phone), both questions stay; before, the second device overwrote the first. An open page fetches what other devices added as soon as it is in front again and every 30 seconds (only changed ones, at most 120 requests per minute and profile). Only deleting replaces the Spark's copy. Questions from the Pebble watch are kept like Siri, Telegram and the companion as their own conversation per day ("Uhr 12.10."). Guests keep their history in their own browser only.

head: The panel

text: - *Instant history sync*: each open page keeps one event connection to the Spark (/api/profile/convos/stream, at most 8 per profile, renewed after 30 minutes). When a conversation changes on another device, the page fetches it at once; a deleted conversation closes. While another device answers in the open conversation, a pale "Phone is answering …" shows (only the kind of device, never the question). The live view shows only the number of these connections. - *One conversation for all channels*: Telegram, Siri, the companion, the watch and the own voice at a speaker write into today's main conversation (the newest of today that belongs to no channel alone; else "Heute DD.MM."), each message marked with its channel. More context, but also more foreign context. A voice that is not surely the owner's stays in the speaker's conversation. - *Read history offline*: only a browser the profile trusts at the second sign-in step keeps a copy of the last 30 conversations and the page itself. Without a connection to the Spark the panel opens it for reading; questions without a connection (at most 10) go out once the Spark answers again.
