head: Only the models (without the web panel)
title: Only the models (without the web panel)
text: Then it asks which models (speech recognition Qwen3-ASR 1.7B, 0.6B, Parakeet or none; speech output Qwen3-TTS 0.6B, 1.7B or none; VoiceDesign yes or no, each with a rough memory estimate) and whether the APIs should be reachable from the network or only on the Spark itself (127.0.0.1, e.g. behind your own reverse proxy). An API key is always generated and required. Later runs and updates do not ask again. Without questions:

head: Only the models (without the web panel)
title: Only the models (without the web panel)
text: At the end the addresses, the key and ready-made curl examples are printed and kept in /etc/speech-spark/connection.txt (readable by root only). Without the panel, the speech-spark command does its jobs:

head: Only the models (without the web panel)
title: Only the models (without the web panel)
text: The watchdog for hung services, which otherwise runs in the panel, runs as speech-spark-watch with the same rules. After an update, TTS speaks a sentence and ASR has to understand it; if that fails, the update puts the previous version back. The self-tests run before every update in both modes. The chat model (qwen38) is not part of this repo and is not touched. If Open WebUI runs in Docker on the same Spark, the APIs have to be reachable from the network (127.0.0.1 inside the container is the container itself).

head: Updating
title: Updating
text: In the panel under System you see the installed version and, when GitHub has a newer one, the list of changes. Update installieren (install update) fetches and installs it. Settings, models and voices are kept, and the log streams live. Update abbrechen cancels a running update. Packages that are already installed are not upgraded; only what the new version needs is added. The self-test runs before the new version goes live. If it or an earlier step (download, packages) fails, the update stops and the services keep running the old version unchanged. If something fails after the switch, update.sh installs the previous version again and says so in the log. While the update runs, a progress window locks the panel (other tabs and phones too: the server refuses changes, the assistant keeps answering); the page reconnects across the panel restart and reloads when done. After 20 minutes without finishing it offers Reload and Cancel.

head: Updating
title: What's new (changelog)
text: What's new (changelog): every change up to the installed version, one line per version, newest first, with a search. Open it with "Was ist neu" (What's new) at the bottom next to the version number or under *Settings → Update und Sicherung (update and backup) → Was ist neu (Changelog) → View*. The admin and every profile in its own browser login can see it (not guests, not device keys). Versions newer than at the last opening in this browser carry "new". The list comes from CHANGELOG.md of the installed version (the update puts a copy into app/).

head: Updating
title: Updating
text: The installer keeps its own git checkout in /opt/speech-spark/src, so it no longer matters where you cloned the repo originally.

head: Updating
title: Once, for installs from before the update button
text: Once, for installs from before the update button: run git pull and sudo ./install.sh in the cloned repo. After that the button works.

head: Updating
title: Updating
text: Running the script again updates the code and adds what is missing to the Python environments; packages already installed stay as they are. The existing configuration is kept and new settings are added.

head: iPhone app "Spark"
title: iPhone app "Spark"
text: An own app for the iPhone (source in ios/): press the button, ask, the answer comes in the Spark voice, also with the screen locked. "Hey Siri, Ask Spark" (German phrase "Frag Spark") runs through the app without a shortcut, also with AirPods and through Siri in the car. CarPlay as its own icon in the car is planned and needs Apple's approval.

head: Switch it on in the panel
title: Switch it on in the panel
text: 1. Admin: Features → iPhone app on, save. 2. Profile: Me → iPhone app → "iPhone app for me" on. 3. To switch lights and devices from the app: "Smart home from the app" on. The code word applies as everywhere. 4. For the wake word and stand mode: "Allow listening all the time" on. 5. To start routes and calls by voice: "Routes and calls on the iPhone" on. 6. Notes on its own (morning briefing, reminders) come when "On its own" is on for the profile. Reminders and timers ring as iPhone notifications, also with the app closed.

head: Getting the app onto the iPhone (on a Mac, about 15 minutes once)
title: Getting the app onto the iPhone (on a Mac, about 15 minutes once)
text: 1. Install Xcode from the Mac App Store (free) and open it once. 2. Xcode → Settings → Accounts → + → sign in with your Apple ID. A free account is enough to try it; the app then runs for 7 days and has to be installed again. With the Apple Developer Program (99 €/year) it runs for a year and works with TestFlight. 3. Get the repo: git clone https://github.com/db9979/speech-on-dgx-spark.git (or git pull). 4. Double-click ios/Spark.xcodeproj. 5. Click the project Spark → target Spark → Signing & Capabilities → pick your account as Team. Do the same for the second target SparkNotify (it fetches the text of push notifications). If Xcode says the bundle ID is taken: project Spark (not the target) → Build Settings → search APP_BUNDLE_ID and add something of your own; both targets take it over. 6. Connect the iPhone by cable, unlock it, confirm "Trust This Computer". 7. On the iPhone: Settings → Privacy & Security → Developer Mode on (the iPhone restarts). 8. In Xcode pick your iPhone as the destination at the top, then press ▶︎ (Run). 9. On first start the iPhone says "Untrusted Developer": Settings → General → VPN & Device Management → your Apple ID → Trust. Then open the app.

head: Pairing
title: Pairing
text: 1. In the panel Me → iPhone app → "Pair an iPhone". 2. On a PC: scan the QR code with the iPhone camera. On the iPhone: tap "open in the app". 3. The app asks "Pair with this Spark?" and shows the address. Tap Pair only for your own address.

head: Pairing
title: Pairing
text: The link is valid for 10 minutes and once. The address must be https with a real certificate (your reverse proxy); the self-signed certificate on port 31443 is not accepted.

head: Pairing
title: With an invitation
text: With an invitation (since V01.0.276): when someone without a profile opens the invitation link on the iPhone and taps "Rather straight in the iPhone app", the app creates the profile with name and PIN and is paired right away. The app shows the Spark's address first. An app that is already paired takes no invitation (unpair first); PIN links work only in the browser.

head: Using it
title: Using it
text: - The assistant's face at the top is the same as in the panel (robot or comic, picked by the admin under Settings → Defaults; the app takes it over when it opens). It blinks, looks around, listens with a red antenna, thinks with a turning arc and moves its mouth while speaking. Tapping it works like the button. With "Face shows what it does" on in the panel (V01.0.323), the app's face shows the same as the panel: a magnifier while searching, a calendar sheet, a letter, a light bulb for the smart home, a note pad when remembering, think bubbles, a tick with a wink after something was done, a question mark on an error and "zzz" after 5 quiet minutes. Driven only by the Spark's events, never by the answer's text. - Big button: tap, speak; the app notices when you are done (or tap again). Tapping while the Spark speaks stops it. - Questions can also be typed. Top left starts a new conversation; after 10 minutes of quiet it starts anew by itself.

head: Using it
title: Using it
text: Routes and calls: "Navigiere zur Arbeit" or "Ruf Anna an". The app asks every time ("Open route to …?", "Call Anna (number)?"). Only "Ja" (tapped or said) opens Maps or calls. Contacts are searched only on the iPhone; the number does not go to the Spark.

head: Quick start, history, photos, offline
title: Quick start, history, photos, offline
text: - Quick start: "Talk to Spark" opens the app and it listens at once. On the Action button: iPhone Settings → Action Button → Shortcut → "Talk to Spark". In Control Center (iOS 18 and later) via "Add a Control", on the lock screen as a widget. With Siri: "Hey Siri, Start Spark". - History: The clock icon at the top left shows your earlier conversations, the same list as the panel's log. Tapping one continues it. Deleting stays in the panel. - Today (since V01.0.286): the sun at the top right shows what is due today, like *Me → Today* in the panel: next appointments of today and tomorrow, open reminders, unread messages, documents, remembered facts. Only cards of functions your profile may use; pull down to refresh. - Ask about a photo or document: The paper clip next to the input: take a photo, choose a photo, or a document (PDF, text, image). The iPhone reads the text itself, scanned pages too. Only the text goes to the Spark. The attachment stays for the conversation until you remove it with ✕. Let the Spark look at photos: with "Let the model look at photos from the app" on under Me → iPhone app (plus the admin and profile switches for pictures), a photo goes to the Spark as a pi

head: Quick start, history, photos, offline
title: Quick start, history, photos, offline
text: cture, scaled to 1280 px, so it also recognises things, plants or an error display. Follow-up questions about the same photo work for 10 minutes. With it off, the iPhone reads only the text as before. PDFs and documents always stay text. - Save to "My documents": With "Store documents from the app" on under Me → iPhone app in the panel, the attachment shows a button for it. The Spark then finds the document later, like an upload in the panel. - Offline: When the Spark cannot be reached, the app says so at the top. Typed questions wait (at most 10, for one day) and go out once the Spark is back. Speaking does not work then, because the Spark recognises the speech. - English: On an iPhone set to English the app is in English, including the wake word and Siri ("Ask Spark", "Start Spark").

head: My profile
title: My profile
text: In the app under Settings → My profile you set the same values as in the panel; changes apply on both sides at once:

head: My profile
title: My profile
text: - Voice: voice and speaking speed, with "Listen to a sample". - Answers: answer length. Your wishes for the tone are only shown; they change in the panel, because the language model is told them. - By itself: on/off, quiet time, at most so many notes a day, appointments with lead time, weather with place and time, parcels, birthdays, bus and train, greeting, mails, morning briefing with time. Shown only when the admin has "By itself" on. Topics whose service is off in the profile are greyed out. - What the app may do: shown only. Change it in the panel under Me → iPhone app.

head: Reminders, sharing, Shortcuts
title: Reminders, sharing, Shortcuts
text: - Apple Reminders: With "Apple Reminders on the iPhone" (Me → iPhone app, off) the app asks after each Spark reminder "… also put into the Reminders app?". After "yes" it is in the list "Spark", without its own alarm (the Spark rings already). When the Spark cancels a reminder it goes there too. New shopping and to-do entries come into the lists "Shopping" and "To-dos" when the app opens (each entry once). A list kept in a CalDAV account stays there. - Share → Spark: In Safari, Mail, Files or Photos tap Share → Spark. Text, web page (the iPhone loads it itself), PDF or photo: the iPhone reads the text (a photo goes as a picture with the photo switch on), then you ask about it or store it under "My documents" (with the documents switch). The answer can be shared, e.g. as a note. - Shortcuts: The Shortcuts app gets "Ask Spark", "Reminder at the Spark", "Add to a Spark list" and "Store a document at the Spark". Lists need the reminders switch, documents the documents switch. - Notes: Apple does not let apps write into Notes directly. Two ways: long-press an answer in the app → "Share (e.g. as a note)", or a shortcut of "Ask Spark" plus Apple's "Create Note".

head: Panel areas in the app
title: Panel areas in the app
text: The app takes over the panel bit by bit (plan "iPhone app takes over the panel"). The admin switches on "Panel areas in the iPhone app" under Features, and each profile switches on each area on its own under Me → iPhone app. Everything starts off, guests get none of it. The app itself cannot switch an area on.

head: Panel areas in the app
title: Panel areas in the app
text: - Open in the panel (Settings): whatever the app does not show itself opens the panel in Safari at the right place (memory, e-mail, security …). With "Manage the Spark" also monitoring, logs, features and profiles. Pages whose functions the admin switched off entirely say "Switched off by the admin" (since V01.0.276, from the same list /api/features as the panel). - Features and People and devices under Manage the Spark (since V01.0.276): the names and groups of the switches come from the Spark, the app keeps no list of its own. A profile also shows its functions "n of m on" to switch, its admin role and the signed-in browsers (swipe to sign out). - My day (switch "My day in the app"): the next appointments of your calendars, the Spark's reminders (swipe to delete) and the memory (look at it, delete single entries, ask for a tidy-up and apply it). Under My profile the conversation switches join: learn from conversations, a new conversation every day and, when the admin allows them, learn from corrections, think when choosing tools and targeted tool choice. Forgetting everything at once stays in the browser. - Manage the Spark (switch "Manage the Spark in the app"): after Face ID yo

head: Panel areas in the app
title: Panel areas in the app
text: u sign in with the admin password and the admin's code, as in the browser. Without the admin's second login step the Spark refuses this sign-in from an iPhone. The sign-in lasts only while the app is open. Inside: Monitoring ("Needs you", memory, CPU/GPU, services), Logs (diagnosis as in the panel with areas and time span, "Copy for thread" and share) and Checks (function check, quality test, priority check). Under Change (V01.0.250): Features (the plain on/off switches; sensitive ones like "Port", the second login step for profiles and the iPhone switches themselves stay in the browser), People and devices (create a profile, remove devices, new PIN, reset the second step, delete a profile; the last three with a code) and Backups (back up now, delete old ones; restoring and downloading in the browser). If your profile has an admin role (co-admin or manager, V01.0.256), there is also "Sign in with my profile": with your profile's code instead of the admin password, ending after 15 minutes without use. A manager sees only monitoring, logs, features and profiles and devices; a co-admin does not delete backups. - Manage documents (switch "Manage documents in the app", V01.0.250): in "M

head: Panel areas in the app
title: Panel areas in the app
text: y documents" swipe to delete, long-press for "For everyone", searching on/off, tags, read again and "Remind me of the deadline". At the bottom "Document switches" with the switches of Me → Documents, as far as the admin allows them. - Teach your voice (switch "Teach your voice in the app"): the app shows three sentences, you read them aloud, saving needs the code from the authenticator app. Below, "Teach" for each of your speakers (the speaker then asks for five sentences). Needs speaker recognition from the admin and your profile's second login step. - Proactive (switch "Proactive in the app"): weather place, parcels from e-mails, bus and train (search and set a stop), look at and stop your jobs, room mode "+30 min" (at most four hours from now). The switches weather, parcels, bus and train and jobs are here too. - Security (switch "Security in the app"): your devices (swipe to remove), recent logins, log out everywhere, turn the second step off or new recovery codes (with a code). Setting it up works only in the browser with the PIN: otherwise someone with your unlocked iPhone alone could set their own second step. - Connect accounts (switch "Connect accounts in the app"): mail,

head: Panel areas in the app
title: Panel areas in the app
text: calendar, contacts, smart home and Telegram. Only with your profile's second login step and a fresh code. The Spark checks the connection, stores password or token encrypted and never hands it out; the iPhone does not keep it.

head: Looking at my documents
title: Looking at my documents
text: With "Documents from the app" (Me → iPhone app), Settings → My documents lists your documents on the Spark, with search. Tap one to open it: a kept PDF or picture opens in Apple's preview (zoom, search, share), and the "Text" tab shows the text the Spark stored. Other file types show as text only. Long texts come in parts: "Read on" at the bottom adds the next one. Deleting and more work with "Manage documents in the app" (above).

head: Messages to other profiles
title: Messages to other profiles
text: Since V01.0.479 there is no envelope next to the input any more: you write in Chats (button at the top right when chats are on). The old messages still open from a notification or with Siri, no language model involved. "Ready?" shows whether the admin and your profile allow messages and whom you can reach, with the reason for those you cannot (e.g. "has messages off"). Pick the recipient and write (at most 500 characters); in the inbox swipe right to reply, left to delete. A message notification can be answered in place (long press → "Reply"). Who may write to you is set in the browser only. The app does not read messages aloud by itself; ask the assistant ("Do I have messages?"), also in the car. Voice messages are listed; listen to them in the panel. With Siri: "Message with Spark" asks for recipient and text and confirms before sending; the name must match a profile that takes your messages. With many profiles (V01.0.206) "To" opens a list with a search (name or call name), ★ favourites and recent ones on top; the star keeps a favourite on the Spark. "Ready?" then shows only numbers, the names open on a tap. When several profiles fit for Siri, Siri asks "Whom do you mean?" with

head: Messages to other profiles
title: Messages to other profiles
text: at most 4 names; for an unknown name it says at most 3 similar ones.

head: Where the Spark is listening (room mode)
title: Where the Spark is listening (room mode)
text: Since V01.0.209 the app shows when a device of your profile listens in room mode (browser or speaker). Switch it on in the panel under Me → iPhone app → "Raum-Modus in der App zeigen" (show room mode in the app) (off, needs room mode from the admin). The top of the chat then reads "● Küche hört zu bis 21:30" with "Beenden", with several devices one line that opens a list. The app asks when it opens, when it comes back and every 30 seconds. The lock screen and the Dynamic Island show a Live Activity with the time left and "Beenden" (turn off in the iPhone Settings → Spark → Live Activities). It is only updated while the app runs; after the end time it reads "vorbei" until the app looks again. The "Raum-Modus" widget (home and lock screen) shows "Küche hört zu bis 21:30" or "Niemand hört zu". With Siri: "End room mode with Spark". The app can only end room mode, never start it; it sees only where and until when, never what was heard.

head: Spark update from the app
title: Spark update from the app
text: For chosen profiles, off by default. The admin switches on Features → Spark update from the iPhone app and ticks per profile:

head: Spark update from the app
title: Spark update from the app
text: - Notices: when a new version with green GitHub tests is ready, a notification arrives on the iPhone, once per version and not during the profile's quiet time. Needs "Push to the iPhone app". - Start: the app shows "Update now" under Settings → Spark version, confirmed with Face ID (or the iPhone passcode) and a fresh code from the profile's authenticator app, so "Start" can only be ticked for profiles with the second login step.

head: Spark update from the app
title: Spark update from the app
text: The page shows the installed and the new version with its changes. The update runs as in the panel: a backup, then update.sh, which installs only versions with green tests. The app follows the progress and the restart. At most one start from the app every 10 minutes; the other profiles with notices hear who started it. Going back to the old version stays in the panel (Status → System/Update).

head: Push notifications with the app closed
title: Push notifications with the app closed
text: 1. developer.apple.com → Certificates, IDs & Profiles → Keys → + → tick Apple Push Notifications service (APNs) → Continue → Register → Download. The .p8 file can be downloaded only once. The Key ID is shown next to it, the Team ID under Membership. 2. Panel as admin: Features → Push to the iPhone app on, enter .p8, Key ID, Team ID and the app's bundle ID. Kind of app: "Development" while you install from Xcode, "Production" for TestFlight and the App Store. Save. 3. Profile: Me → iPhone app → "Notifications to the iPhone" on. 4. Open the app once and allow notifications, then "Send a test message" in the panel.

head: Push notifications with the app closed
title: Push notifications with the app closed
text: Then reminders and timers (also those set in the panel or on a speaker), the morning briefing, notes and memory tidying arrive with the app closed. Only "Neue Nachricht vom Spark" goes through Apple; the text stays on the Spark for 24 hours and the app fetches it with its key. With push, reminders no longer ring twice. At most 30 notifications per hour and profile.

head: CarPlay
title: CarPlay
text: An own "Spark" icon in the car. Tap → "Mit Spark sprechen" → talk. The conversation goes on hands-free until 8 seconds of silence; interrupting works as in the app. The car shows only the state, never text. Answers are short in the car. Smart home in the car only with its own switch "Smart home in the car too" and the code word. Route and call only after "Ja".

head: CarPlay
title: Apple must grant CarPlay first
text: Apple must grant CarPlay first: request the category "Voice-based conversational app" at developer.apple.com/contact/carplay. After approval, enable it for the App ID and add <key>com.apple.developer.carplay-voice-based-conversation</key><true/> to ios/Spark.entitlements (not before: without the grant Xcode cannot sign the app). After the grant, try it without a car: Simulator → I/O → External Displays → CarPlay.

head: Security
title: Security
text: - Each iPhone gets its own key when pairing, kept only in that iPhone's keychain and on the Spark only as a hash. - The key may only ask and listen (chat, speech recognition, Siri question). Settings, memory, devices, connections and further pairings are refused. - The profile's switch off locks all its iPhones at once, the admin switch all of them. Remove a lost iPhone under Me → iPhone app → Remove. - Smart home from the app only with its own switch and the code word. What the app claims to be does not count; the panel decides by the key. - Wake word, stand mode, routes and calls only with their own switch in the panel. The Spark only suggests a route or call; the tool exists only for the app key with the switch, and only your "yes" on the iPhone starts it. Outside text (mail, web page) cannot start a route or call. - No sound goes to the Spark before the wake word. In the background the app listens only with the wake word on. - Push: the Apple key (.p8) is stored encrypted, changed only by the admin with the second step, never shown again. Apple only gets a fixed sentence and a random number. Only the app with its own key signs up its push address; a removed iPhone gets nothing

head: Security
title: Security
text: from then on. Only the profile's own app gets a notification's text. - Photos and documents: the iPhone reads the text, only text goes to the Spark (at most 20,000 characters per question). Photos go as pictures only with the photo switch on; a round with a picture offers no tools, and the picture is not kept in the history. The Spark treats it as outside text: it sits as data in the prompt, not in the conversation, and locks actions as after a mail. The history keeps only the attachment's name. - Storing documents only with its own switch, only with the app key, at most 10 per minute and 3 MB. The app cannot list or delete the documents. - "My profile" changes only a fixed list (voice, speed, length, by itself, morning briefing). The app's rights, Telegram, the smart home and the tone cannot be changed through it; a request with any other field is refused as a whole. - Apple Reminders: only with its own switch, only after "yes" on the iPhone. The app reads nothing from Reminders for the Spark. Shortcuts may only add entries to the lists; list settings stay in the panel. - Sharing: shared content is outside text (locks actions), at most 20,000 characters per question; the iPhone lo

head: Security
title: Security
text: ads web pages itself, at most 3 MB. - Waiting questions stay on the iPhone and are deleted when unpairing. - Spark update: only the admin gives the rights (with the admin's code when the second step is on); a profile cannot give them to itself. Starting needs the app's key, Face ID and a fresh 6-digit code of the profile (each code once, wrong codes count towards the lock), at most once in 10 minutes. The app cannot pick a version; only versions with passed GitHub tests are installed. Every start is in the security log, and the language model has no tool for it. - CarPlay never loosens anything: in the car the smart home is locked without its own car switch. - Pairing only from the profile's own browser login, with the second login step when the profile has it. At most 5 iPhones per profile.

head: What the Spark offers for it
title: What the Spark offers for it
text: Every push that changes ios/ builds the app on GitHub for the simulator (.github/workflows/ios.yml), so errors show there and not only in Xcode.

head: Publishing the iPhone app
title: Publishing the iPhone app
text: Three ways, from the simplest to the most work. All need the Apple Developer Program (99 €/year).

head: 1. Once: create the app at Apple
title: 1. Once: create the app at Apple
text: 1. Check in Xcode: project Spark → Build Settings → APP_BUNDLE_ID is your own bundle ID (e.g. io.github.db9979.speechspark.dominik). Both targets (Spark and SparkNotify) have your team selected under Signing & Capabilities. 2. appstoreconnect.apple.com → Apps → + → New App: platform iOS, a name (it must be free in the App Store; "Spark" is surely taken, e.g. "Spark voice assistant"), primary language, the bundle ID from the list, any SKU (e.g. speechspark).

head: 2. Upload every new version
title: 2. Upload every new version
text: 1. git pull in the repo. 2. Xcode → target Spark → General: raise Version (e.g. 1.1) when something changes for users. The Build number counts up by itself: building sets it to the number of commits in the repo, the same for the app and all its extensions, so it is larger after every git pull. The app shows both small at the bottom, e.g. "1.0 (412)". 3. Choose Any iOS Device (arm64) as the destination at the top. 4. Product → Archive. After a few minutes the Organizer opens. 5. Distribute App → App Store Connect → Distribute. Xcode signs and uploads. 6. After 5–30 minutes the build shows in App Store Connect under TestFlight. The app answers the encryption question itself (https only, ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption = NO).

head: 2. Upload every new version
title: 2. Upload every new version
text: Then set the kind to "Production" in the panel under Features → Push to the iPhone app: TestFlight and App Store builds use Apple's production push. Installed straight from Xcode it is "Development" again.

head: Upload with the GitHub button "TestFlight"
title: Upload with the GitHub button "TestFlight"
text: Instead of Archive and Distribute on the Mac this also works on GitHub. The button builds the app, lets Apple sign it and uploads it to TestFlight. It starts only for a commit whose tests passed. The build number counts up by itself.

head: Upload with the GitHub button "TestFlight"
title: Upload with the GitHub button "TestFlight"
text: Once: 1. App Store Connect → Users and Access → Integrations → App Store Connect API → Team Keys: create a key with role Admin. Only Admin may fetch certificates for signing. If you already have an App Manager key for the texts, replace it with this one. 2. GitHub → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions: ASC_KEY_ID, ASC_ISSUER_ID, ASC_KEY (the whole content of the .p8 file) and also ASC_TEAM_ID (developer.apple.com → Membership → Team ID).

head: Upload with the GitHub button "TestFlight"
title: Upload with the GitHub button "TestFlight"
text: Then: GitHub → Actions → TestFlight → Run workflow, enter the bundle ID, Run. After 15 to 30 minutes the build is in App Store Connect under TestFlight.

head: Upload with the GitHub button "TestFlight"
title: Automatic
text: Automatic: when a commit on main changes something under ios/, TestFlight starts by itself as soon as "iPhone app" and "Tests" passed. At most one upload per hour. If a newer iOS commit comes in the waiting time, only that one is uploaded. If a newer push cancelled the tests of the iOS commit, the newest main commit with passed tests that contains the iOS commit goes up (V01.0.321). The certificates a run makes for itself are revoked again at its end, otherwise Apple's limit is reached after some dozen runs ("reached the maximum number of certificates", V01.0.334). If that message still shows in a run, revoke the old entries under developer.apple.com → Certificates. Turn it off: GitHub → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables → TESTFLIGHT_AUTO = off. A bundle ID other than io.github.db9979.speechspark goes into the variable APP_BUNDLE_ID. To start again always use Run workflow, not "Re-run", because a re-run builds the old commit.

head: Upload with the GitHub button "TestFlight"
title: Upload with the GitHub button "TestFlight"
text: If it does not work the first time, send the red line from the run.

head: 3. TestFlight (recommended for you and the family)
title: 3. TestFlight (recommended for you and the family)
text: 1. App Store Connect → Users and Access: invite family members with their Apple ID (a role like "Marketing" is enough). 2. App → TestFlight → Internal Testing → + → create a group "Family", add the people, assign the build. 3. Everybody installs the TestFlight app from the App Store on the iPhone and accepts the invitation. New builds arrive there by themselves.

head: 3. TestFlight (recommended for you and the family)
title: 3. TestFlight (recommended for you and the family)
text: A TestFlight build runs 90 days; then simply upload a new one.

head: 4. App Store (only when strangers should load the app)
title: 4. App Store (only when strangers should load the app)
text: In addition to steps 1–2, in App Store Connect under the app:

head: 4. App Store (only when strangers should load the app)
title: 4. App Store (only when strangers should load the app)
text: - Screenshots: at least for 6.9" (iPhone 16 Pro Max) or 6.5", from the simulator with ⌘S. - Description, keywords, support URL (e.g. the GitHub page). - Privacy policy (URL): ready in app-privacy.md, German in app-datenschutz.md. Enter the GitHub link of the file as the URL. - App Privacy: "Data Not Collected" (everything goes to the user's own Spark, not to you). Notifications through Apple carry only a fixed sentence. - Age rating: fill in the questionnaire (no content of the categories → 4+; because of the free answers of a language model rather 12+). - Notes for the review: Apple's reviewers need a Spark. Create a test profile of its own, make a pairing link (it lasts only 10 minutes, so better add a short video of the app and offer to send a link on request) and name the address of your reverse proxy. - Availability: request "Unlisted" (by link only) at Apple when the app should not show up in the App Store search.

head: Fill in the texts automatically
title: Fill in the texts automatically
text: Name, subtitle, promotional text, description, keywords, URLs and categories (German and English) are in ios/fastlane/metadata. A button on GitHub writes them into App Store Connect. It uploads no build and no pictures and submits nothing for review.

head: Fill in the texts automatically
title: Fill in the texts automatically
text: 1. The app must already exist in App Store Connect (step 1), with German as the primary language. 2. App Store Connect → Users and Access → Integrations → App Store Connect API → Team Keys → +: name "GitHub texts", role App Manager. Download the .p8 file (works only once), note the Key ID and the Issuer ID. 3. GitHub → repo → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret, three times: ASC_KEY_ID (Key ID), ASC_ISSUER_ID (Issuer ID), ASC_KEY (the whole content of the .p8 file). 4. GitHub → Actions → App Store texts → Run workflow: enter bundle ID, version (1.0) and copyright (e.g. 2026 First Last), Run. 5. After about 2 minutes the texts are in App Store Connect. You can revoke the key there afterwards.

head: Fill in the texts automatically
title: Fill in the texts automatically
text: The screenshots (German and English, 6.9" and 6.3") are made by the workflow App Store screenshots in the iPhone simulator with example content. It puts them on the branch app-store-screenshots. With the box "upload screenshots too" ticked, App Store texts enters them as well. The demo mode (-SparkDemo) exists only in the test build, not in the app from the store.

head: Fill in the texts automatically
title: Fill in the texts automatically
text: Left by hand: App Privacy, age rating, notes for the review and price. The answers for them are in the project's papers ("App Store Connect: Angaben für Spark").

head: Fill in the texts automatically
title: Fill in the texts automatically
text: Then Submit for Review. The review usually takes 1–3 days. A frequent rejection: the reviewer gets no further because they have no Spark (guideline 2.1), hence the video and the test access.

head: CarPlay
title: CarPlay
text: Builds with CarPlay can only be uploaded once Apple granted the CarPlay entitlement and it is entered in ios/Spark.entitlements (see iphone-app.md). Until then upload builds without that line; everything else works.

head: Security
title: Security
text: - Assistant without password: off on new installs. Then only profiles (name and PIN) and devices with a key reach the assistant. Switch under *Settings → Security*. - Lockout after wrong attempts: after 5 wrong passwords or PINs from one address (or 10 for one profile name or the admin password, from anywhere) the panel waits 1 minute, twice as long with every further lockout, at most an hour. On top, each name gets at most 30 wrong attempts a day. A browser that logged in successfully with that name before is not locked out by a stranger this way, also not on the road with a new address (cookie speech_known). Since V01.0.402 only the browser counts, not the address and not a login with another profile: a housemate with a profile of their own cannot guess another profile's PIN without the lock. The counts survive a restart of the panel and are pruned, so made-up names cannot grow them without end. - Reverse proxy: behind a reverse proxy in the LAN (e.g. Synology) the real address from X-Forwarded-For counts, so one guesser cannot lock everybody out. Enter the proxy's address under *Settings → Security → Adressen des Reverse-Proxys* (reverse proxy addresses); the panel trusts that h

head: Security
title: Security
text: eader only from there. Without an entry it counts only from a proxy on the Spark itself; proxies in the home network then share one address for the lockout (the panel log says "X-Forwarded-For … ignored"). - Logins expire: the admin login after 7 days without use, a profile login after 30 days (7–90 under *Settings → Security → Sign-in in the browser*, since V01.0.262); while in use they renew themselves. Logging out ends the login on the server too. *Me → Security → Log out everywhere* ends the profile's login in all other browsers. On https (also behind the proxy) the cookies are Secure. - Signed-in browsers (since V01.0.262): *Me → Security* lists every browser the profile is signed in to (only a short name like "iPhone · Safari", first and last use, no address), with *Sign out* for each one; the admin sees the same list in the profile details. At most 20 per profile, the oldest ends first. Logins from before V01.0.262 appear after their next use. - Browser protection (since V01.0.262): every panel answer forbids embedding in other pages (X-Frame-Options, frame-ancestors), guessing file types (nosniff), leaking addresses to other sites (Referrer-Policy) and microphone/camera for

head: Security
title: Security
text: anything but the panel (Permissions-Policy); over https Strict-Transport-Security is added. - Strict Content-Security-Policy (since V01.0.286): scripts only run as files from the panel (script-src 'self'): no script in the page, no onclick="…" handlers, no eval. So even injected HTML runs no code. Buttons in generated lists name their function with data-on (base.js ON); only what is registered there can be called. Pictures and sound also from data:/blob: (recordings, QR codes, the face), connections only to the panel itself, no foreign frames. Inline styles stay allowed (they run no code, older Safari versions in the iPhone app need them). The scanner in the self-test turns red on a new inline handler, inline <script>, javascript: link or eval; every browser test counts a CSP message as an error. - Undo (since V01.0.286, plan "Bedienung gesamt" C5): *Status → Logs → Admin log* shows the latest settings changes above the log (when, who, "Weather: off → on") with *Rückgängig* (undo). Kept are the last 50 saved changes from Settings, Features and the iPhone app's switches (state/config-undo.json, only names and short values). Never in it: secrets and addresses that need the admin cod

head: Security
title: Security
text: e (keys, tokens, passwords, the language model address …), the *panel* section (ports, proxies: a wrong value could shut the admin out), lists and long texts. Undo only puts back values still as that change left them (ones changed again since stay and are named), with the same checks and service restarts as saving, and becomes an entry itself. The main admin sees all, a profile in its admin mode its own; managers none. Log: config_undo. Not in the backup (after a restore the old values no longer fit). - Security at a glance (since V01.0.262): at the top of *Settings → Security* a traffic light of fixed checks (admin second step, age of the backup, short PINs, roles without second step, http instead of https, assistant without password, home network addresses, sign-in duration). Red points also show under *Status → Needs you*. Of PINs the panel only notes whether they are shorter than 6 characters, when set and at sign-in. - Second login step (authenticator app): for the admin under *Settings → Security*, for profiles under *Me → Security* once the admin allows it under *Features* (off on new installs; each profile decides for itself). Set up with a QR code; then the login asks for

head: Security
title: Security
text: the six-digit code, plus 10 recovery codes for a lost phone. "Trust this browser" saves the code on your own device (since V01.0.286 see below); "Log out everywhere" (profile) or "Forget trusted browsers" (admin) ends that. While the admin has it on, HTTP Basic no longer works, and changing the password, restoring a backup, creating or moving device keys and changing PINs ask for a code every time. Devices with a key (speakers, Siri, Pebble, phone) need no code. Way back in: admin sudo rm /var/lib/speech-spark/state/mfa-admin.json; the admin resets a profile under *People and devices*. - Fewer codes (since V01.0.289, plan plaene/zweiter-schritt-seltener.md): three things, kept apart by risk. Trusted browsers: whoever ticks "Trust this browser" at sign-in (the browser remembers the tick) enters no code there for the days under *Settings → Security → Vertraute Browser* (7 to 90, default 60); after 30 days without use it asks again. Every trusted browser is listed with a short name, since when, last use and "asks again from" (admin: *Settings → Security → second login step*, profile: *Me → Security*, the admin also in the profile details) and can be removed on its own; at most 10 per

head: Security
title: Security
text: - New people by invitation (since V01.0.276, *People and devices → New people*, off): invitation only, there is no open sign-up. The admin creates an invitation (suggested name, starter pack, valid 1, 7 or 30 days) and gets a link, a QR code and a card to print; the link needs the panel's https address. Every link works once, the Spark keeps only its fingerprint (SHA-256), at most 50 are open, used ones disappear 7 days after acceptance or at once with the deleted profile (its PIN links too), expired ones after 30 days. Wrong codes count towards the lockout; whether a name is taken is only told to someone with a valid code. The PIN needs at least 6 characters. Starter packs ("Familie", "Gast plus", editable) only switch on profile switches of functions the admin has on, never areas of "Spark verwalten". Second step: by default "required for e-mail, documents, jobs"; a profile from an invitation gets these three only after setting up the second sign-in step and cannot switch it off itself afterwards (fixed check in the panel, reason "mfa" under Me and Who may do what). The main admin gets a push message for every new person. The profile details have PIN link (a new PIN by link inste

head: Security
title: Security
text: ad of passing a PIN on; with the second step only with a code) and Remind (push to the person, at most once per hour). Audit log: invite_made, invite_used, invite_pin, invite_app, handoff_login. - "Los geht's" (since V01.0.276): after the invitation, *Me → Los geht's* walks in five steps (welcome, secure, devices, services, done) through everything the profile may use, with direct links to the pages under Me and QR codes for the iPhone app and pairing. The Spark ticks off what is done itself (second step set up, iPhone paired, calendar there …); the browser can only set "later". The admin sees "Einrichten x von y" in the profile list. - Continue on the phone (since V01.0.276, switch under *Neue Personen*): on the computer "Los geht's" shows a QR code (2 minutes, once). The phone then shows a number; on the computer you tap the right one of three numbers, only then is the phone signed in to the same profile. A wrong number ends the attempt. Device keys cannot start a handoff. - Independent review of 11.10.2026 (plan pruefung/unabhaengige-pruefung-2026-10-11.md, V01.0.403): changing the off-site backup needs a fresh code every time, "Back up now" a code. What a voice at a speaker tha

head: Security
title: Security
text: t was not clearly recognised says is kept as "from outside" in the history: the next turn starts locked, and the assistant learns nothing about the owner from it. Answers made from outside text keep that mark at the Pebble watch too. Document cards in the system prompt are cut short; documents shared by other profiles show only file name, kind and tags. Only a speaker's own key opens the speaker connection. A restore by the owner profile leaves the panel password and its second step unchanged. /docs, /redoc and /openapi.json are gone. Guests get only error codes from speech recognition, and reading aloud has its own limits for guests. Removing devices and "Sign out everywhere" from the iPhone app, and "Continue on the phone", need a code when the second step is on. After outside text, "From phone to PC" puts no text into the clipboard and sends only plain links. Own MCP services cannot reach the Spark's service ports via its LAN address either. An MCP client switches nothing when a smart-home code word is set, and MCP actions are only proposed with arguments that are read out in full before the "yes".

head: Securing the repository and releases
title: Securing the repository and releases
text: Since V01.0.390. The GitHub workflows pin every action to a commit (Dependabot proposes updates monthly), only the job that writes a release or build branch may write, and actions/checkout keeps no token. The signing keys (Android keystore, App Store Connect key, Developer ID) live in the environment release, usable only by workflows on main; workflows on other branches cannot see them. The self-test test_workflows keeps it that way.

head: Securing the repository and releases
title: Securing the repository and releases
text: One-time move of the keys: create a fine-grained token for this repository only (Administration, Environments, Secrets: read and write, valid 1 day), store it as repository secret MIGRATE_TOKEN and run the workflow "Schlüssel in Umgebung verschieben". It creates release (main only, no review), copies every key that is set, then deletes the repository copies and MIGRATE_TOKEN. Values never appear in the log.

head: Securing the repository and releases
title: Securing the repository and releases
text: Recommended on GitHub: 2FA with a passkey, a ruleset on main against deletion and force push, read-only workflow permissions, secret scanning with push protection. tars still installs only commits whose tests passed and refuses rewritten history.

head: Device updates and supply chain (since V01.0.407)
title: Device updates and supply chain (since V01.0.407)
text: - Releases only from the environment release: the jobs that publish the speaker firmware and the Windows companion run in the environment release (main only) too; new firmware rolls out to every speaker at night. The ESP-IDF image is pinned to its digest, pebble-tool and Playwright to a fixed version; the Pebble SDK itself still comes as "latest" (its list could not be reached when this version was built). The token for the branch pebble-build goes through an environment variable, never into the Git URL. - Signed manifests (prepared, off): the workflows sign manifest.json (firmware) and begleiter.json (Windows, Mac) with Ed25519 once the secret UPDATE_SIGNING_KEY exists in the environment release, and put <file>.sig into the release. The Spark checks the signature once a public key is listed in app/panel/signatur.py; then it takes nothing unsigned. Without a key nothing changes: GitHub over https plus SHA-256 and size from the manifest. Setting it up: openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519 -out update-key.pem, store the content as secret UPDATE_SIGNING_KEY under *Settings → Environments → release*, run a build and put the public key shown in its log into signatur.KEYS (only once all th

head: Device updates and supply chain (since V01.0.407)
title: Device updates and supply chain (since V01.0.407)
text: ree releases carry a .sig). Keep update-key.pem offline afterwards. - Speaker updates over https: over http someone in the home network could hand the board a foreign firmware. With *Settings → Security → Lautsprecher-Updates auch über http* switched off (on by default so existing speakers keep updating; changing it needs a code), a speaker that reaches the Spark over http gets no update over Wi-Fi (diagnosis: "nicht über http angeboten"), and the night round skips it; updating over USB in the browser always works. A known board id from another board (different MAC) gets nothing, the key after the code goes only to the address that showed the code, and a wrong challenge at activation is refused. - Companion: the Windows and Mac companions load updates only over https. A Mac companion signed with a Developer ID takes only an update from the same team (codesign -R with the Team ID from its own signature); an ad-hoc signed one checks size, SHA-256, bundle id and a valid signature as before. - iPhone app: a pairing link to another Spark asks explicitly "Switch to another Spark?" with both addresses; unsent messages do not go along when switching. - root and units: install.sh and update

head: Device updates and supply chain (since V01.0.407)
title: Device updates and supply chain (since V01.0.407)
text: .sh read config.json, the update progress, the engine signatures and update-target only as the service user (as_svc cat). The API watchdog (speech-spark-watch) has MemoryMax=1G and PrivateTmp=yes; the vLLM engines deliberately have no MemoryMax (shared GPU memory). - Speech services without an API key: with an empty api.key, ASR and TTS answer only the Spark itself. An old configuration that listens in the network without a key gets a new one at the update. - ffmpeg and speech recognition: every ffmpeg call reads only files and pipes (-protocol_whitelist file,pipe); a playlist fetches nothing from the network. The ASR service waits at its gate before it reads a recording (up to 200 MB) into memory; Parakeet decodes one recording at a time, with two threads and a time limit. - Telegram voice messages are downloaded like photos: streamed, cut off after 5 MB, the file path from Telegram checked. - Spark update: if /etc/speech-spark-signers exists but is not a plain file of root (a link, another owner, writable by others), the update stops instead of quietly skipping the check. Without the file the update log says "Signature check off". To switch it on: sign commits with an SSH key (gi

head: Device updates and supply chain (since V01.0.407)
title: Device updates and supply chain (since V01.0.407)
text: t config gpg.format ssh, user.signingkey, commit.gpgsign true) and create /etc/speech-spark-signers (root, 644) on the Spark with <e-mail> <public key>; from then on tars installs only signed commits.

head: Kill switch (Notaus)
title: Kill switch (Notaus)
text: The red "Notaus" button (bottom of the sidebar, on phones at the top of Manage) stops the Spark in three stages. Triggering needs no code and only goes up; lifting is for admins only.

head: Kill switch (Notaus)
title: Kill switch (Notaus)
text: - Who triggers: only admins (main admin, co-admin, manager in admin mode), also from the iPhone app in admin mode and on the way (since V01.0.338; before, a switch could allow it for every profile). Ordinary profiles see neither the button nor the band nor the Status card; only in stage 3 or from outside a page "The Spark is stopped right now" without a name or reason. Never guests, MCP or the language model; Telegram, voice, Home Assistant and the Android tile only as described under *Other ways* below (since V01.0.360). - Lifting: only the main admin or a profile in its admin mode (owner, co-admin), only in a browser (no app key, no HTTP Basic), only in the home network, with a fresh code (without a second step: the panel password again). Choice: back to stage 1 or off; held jobs then run on or are cancelled (default). - Home network means a direct connection from a private network. Through a reverse proxy only what a listed proxy (Settings → Security → Reverse proxy) passes on as a home address counts; a listed proxy without that counts as outside. So list the proxy there. - Kept across restart and update (state/notaus.json). A damaged file counts as stage 3, never as off. Way o

head: Kill switch (Notaus)
title: Kill switch (Notaus)
text: ut without the panel: sudo rm /var/lib/speech-spark/state/notaus.json. - Visible: red band on every page, a card under Status (kinds and counts since it was triggered, never contents), a push to the admin profiles when triggered and lifted, an entry in the admin log. Status → Live and the live monitor /live show a red band with stage, time, channel and per kind "held" with a count (never the reason or a name) and keep running in stage 3 (reading only; pairing a new monitor waits). - ESP32 speakers (firmware build 6 and later, since V01.0.368): hold the BOOT button for 5 seconds. The firmware then sends the fixed wake word "spark-notaus" (only the button sends it, never speech recognition). Only a speaker of an admin profile triggers the big emergency stop, stage 2, and announces it; otherwise it says "only for an admin's speaker". Never *My kill switch*: a button press does not say who pressed it. - Pebble watch (watch app 1.6.0 and later, since V01.0.368): hold SELECT for 3 seconds until it buzzes long, then let go. The watch sends the fixed sentence "Spark, Notaus" (as above: the big one only for admin profiles). "Spark, Mein Notaus" works by dictation. - iPhone app (since V01.0.

head: Kill switch (Notaus)
title: Kill switch (Notaus)
text: 370, with the next TestFlight build): emergency stop button behind a question and the Siri shortcut "Spark Notaus"; without admin mode only *My kill switch*, never lifting in the app. - Emergency stop by itself (since V01.0.368, switch under *Settings → Security*, off; changing it needs the admin code): the guard switches on stage 1 "Outside closed" by fixed rules, never higher: 20 wrong sign-ins, PINs, codes or emergency stop keys from outside in 10 minutes; an MCP flood from outside (30 MCP requests turned away by the rate limit in 10 minutes); 15 connections refused by netguard in 10 minutes (such as 169.254.x, home addresses or the Spark's own services, where outside text tries to steer the Spark; refusals by the emergency stop itself do not count). Counted in memory only. Channel "Wächter" in the push, the admin log and Status → Live; lifting as always.

head: Other ways to the emergency stop (since V01.0.360)
title: Other ways to the emergency stop (since V01.0.360)
text: All of these only switch on, never off; lifting stays in the browser. The panel always decides by fixed rules, never the language model and never text from outside.

head: Other ways to the emergency stop (since V01.0.360)
title: Other ways to the emergency stop (since V01.0.360)
text: - Telegram: /meinnotaus stops the own profile (like *My kill switch*; afterwards Telegram only answers "Mein Notaus ist an"). /notaus (stage 2) or /notaus 1–/notaus 3 only for profiles with an admin role; forwarded messages never count as a command. From stage 1 on Telegram itself rests. - Fixed sentence in the chat, by voice on the phone, in the app or at a speaker that recognised the voice: "Spark, Mein Notaus" for every profile, "Spark, Notaus" (stage 2) or "Spark, Notaus Stufe eins/zwei/drei" only for admin profiles. Only the whole sentence, no question about it ("Was ist der Notaus?" triggers nothing). Never over MCP, never for a voice the speaker does not recognise as the profile. - Home Assistant: *Settings → Security → Emergency stop from outside* creates a key (fresh admin code, at most 5, only the hash in state/notaus-keys.json, plain text shown once) with ready text for configuration.yaml: rest_command.spark_notaus (POST /api/notaus/ha, Authorization: Bearer …, {"level": 1–3}, default 2) and a REST sensor on /api/notaus with the stage. Home network only; the key reads nothing, lifts nothing and is no device key. Wrong keys lock like wrong logins, rate limit notausha. - A

head: Other ways to the emergency stop (since V01.0.360)
title: Other ways to the emergency stop (since V01.0.360)
text: ndroid tile (Android app 1.1.0 and later): add "Notaus" in quick settings. It uses the login of the app's page; admins choose "Ganzer Spark" (stage 2) or "Mein Notaus", everyone else only "Mein Notaus", always behind a question. The tile shows the stage. - The channel shows in the admin log, the push and on Status → Live (telegram, sprache, ha, android).

head: My kill switch (own profile only)
title: My kill switch (own profile only)
text: Since V01.0.338 every signed-in profile has its own, weaker kill switch under *Me → Security → My kill switch* (admins have it besides the big one). It stops only this profile; the others notice nothing:

head: My kill switch (own profile only)
title: My kill switch (own profile only)
text: - Ways in closed: every other browser login ends (the browser that triggered it stays signed in); the profile's device keys (iPhone and Android app, Siri, watch, speakers, Home Assistant events) only get "locked", as do MCP keys, OAuth access and Telegram. - Nothing in its name: smart home, mail drafts and tidying, messages and announcements, appointments, lists, reMarkable, MCP actions; no "yes" carries anything out; jobs wait in the queue; "on its own", Home Assistant notes and briefings of the profile stay silent. - Reading stays (Dominik's choice 3b): in its own browser the profile still asks and may read mail, calendar, memory and documents. - Lifting: the profile itself, only in the browser (no app key), with its PIN (wrong tries lock like at sign-in) and a fresh code when its second step is on; or an admin under *Status → Profiles' own kill switch* (same rules as the big one). The admin profiles get a push with the name, never a reason. - File: state/notaus-mine.json. A damaged file holds every profile, and only an admin lifts that. Status → Live shows only how many profiles, never which.

head: Reporting problems
title: Reporting problems
text: Since V01.0.386. Something does not work? Every profile with its own switch (Me → Reporting problems) describes it briefly and gets a draft; guests never. Admin switch: Features → Security → "Reporting problems", plus the target repository (default db9979/spark-meldungen, private). It opens everywhere: "Report a problem" at the bottom of the panel, Status → Logs, Ctrl/⌘ K, Me → Reporting problems, in the Android app (panel), in the iPhone app under Settings, in the Spark companion (Windows: the icon's menu; Mac: settings), by Telegram /melden text and by voice (also watch and speakers) with the fixed sentence "Spark, Problem melden: …". Telegram and voice only make a draft; sending always comes after a look at the preview.

head: Reporting problems
title: What goes along
text: What goes along: the description, if wanted the own last requests (only ways, tools, times from Logs → Requests), the system state (version, services, memory), from the iPhone app the sound log, and for admins only diagnose log lines of the area (10, 30 or 60 min).

head: Reporting problems
title: Anonymizing
text: Anonymizing: fixed rules on the Spark, no language model. First the log redaction, then secrets (everything in the vault, tokens, passwords) become [GEHEIM], contents in log lines (quotes, subject, question, search, appointment, file name …) [INHALT], addresses [URL], [MAIL], [IP-LAN], [IP], [HOST], places [ORT], phone numbers [TELEFON], long identifiers [ID], profile, device and account names [PERSON-1], [GERÄT-1], [KONTO-1] (same number for the same name). Code blocks and @ cannot trigger anything. Only the anonymized version is stored, 14 days.

head: Reporting problems
title: Preview and sending
text: Preview and sending: the Spark shows title and text exactly as they go out; lines can be unticked. Only what matches the preview is sent (a signature over the text); a leak check blocks sending while a known name, a mail address, an address or a secret is still in it. Three ways: "Send to GitHub" (issue via api.github.com), "Open in the browser" (GitHub with the text filled in, works without a token) and "Keep locally only". Limits: per profile 20 open drafts and 10 new a day, 3 sent per profile and 10 per day, one minute apart.

head: Reporting problems
title: Token
text: Token: a fine-grained token for the report repository only with "Issues: Read and write", 90 days. Only the main admin saves it with a fresh code (Features → Reporting problems), sealed in the vault, never shown, never logged; classic ghp_ tokens are refused. "Check" shows the expiry date and warns when the repository is public; 14 days before expiry a hint shows on Status → Live.

head: Reporting problems
title: Admin view
text: Admin view: admins see every report of every profile, for sent ones the state on GitHub (open or done), the number of answers and the answers themselves as plain text with a link; a profile sees only its own. Answers from GitHub never go to the language model.

head: Reporting problems
title: Tell the admin through the assistant
text: Tell the admin through the assistant (since V01.0.386, sub-switch, off): when a profile sends or keeps a report, the assistant tells the admin profiles (the one chosen for admin notes, the main admin, co-admins), in the assistant when the page is open, else as a note. Only profile name, area, way and number, never the text; the reporting profile itself gets nothing. Every admin profile turns it off for itself under Me → Reporting problems; during the Notaus it stays silent.

head: Reporting problems
title: Live
text: Live: Status → Live shows GitHub (reports) with the number of drafts and of those sent today, never contents.

head: Stability
title: Stability
text: - Backups: every day, before every update, before going back to the previous version and before every restore the panel backs up profiles (memory, conversations, documents, calendars, mail accounts, smart home, speaker ID), cloned voices, settings, the panel password and the shared state of the Spark (the admin's second login step, iPhone push key and devices, Telegram bot, browser push key, ESP32 speakers, agent services, own test questions) to /var/lib/speech-spark/backups. Counted separately, the newest seven daily or manual ones and the newest five from before an update, rollback or restore are kept. *Settings → Update and backup → Backup* downloads, restores or deletes each one and restores a downloaded file. A restore checks the settings like the settings page does, caps the size and swaps all parts or none; the current state is backed up first. Passwords and tokens are in the backup encrypted, the key is not: on another Spark they have to be entered again. An admin second login step the Spark cannot read is then not taken over (the current one stays). For a move there is the move backup: it also carries the key, encrypted with a password you type (at least 12 characters, scr

head: Stability
title: Stability

head: Stability
title: Stability
text: Every install and update runs the panel's self-test (app/tests) against fake LLM, TTS and Home Assistant servers in a throw-away directory: login and access, that profiles never see each other's memory, documents, conversations, mailboxes or Home Assistant, the chat tools, learning from conversations, calendar and text cleaning. It runs before the new version goes live. In an update a failure stops the update and the old version keeps running; on a first install it is only reported. The result is in the update log. It includes the security checks (test_hardening.py, one test per guard) and a scanner (test_scanner.py) that refuses new code using shell=True, eval or the like, a route without a login, an upload read without a size limit, values in onclick not escaped for JavaScript, or an assistant tool not sorted as "reads outside text / changes something / own data only". By hand: cd /opt/speech-spark/app && sudo /opt/speech-spark/venv-panel/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

head: Stability
title: Gentle updates
text: Gentle updates (from V01.0.379): when the update installs exactly the version whose GitHub test run passed, the Spark only runs a smoke test (tests/test_rauchtest.py, a few seconds: every module loads with this Spark's packages, the panel starts and answers). The whole self-test still runs on a first install, with --newest, --to and when going back to the previous version. Both run with the lowest CPU and disk priority (nice 19, ionice class 2/7), so an answer being spoken keeps its speed. An update asks apt only when a package is missing, pip only when the package list or the lock file changed (.pkgs or .locked in the environment), and downloads models only when other ones are chosen (/opt/speech-spark/.models). The ASR and TTS services restart only when something they run from changed: their files per app/restart-map, their systemd unit, the settings or their Python packages; a service the list does not know always restarts, and the smoke test checks the list against the imports. VoiceDesign, like the engines, restarts only when its settings changed. The panel restarts on every update (about 8 s).

head: Stability
title: Install overnight
text: Install overnight (Settings → Update, off): a new tested version is installed at night between 3 and 5 am, at most once a night, with a backup first. If somebody is talking with the Spark (within the last two minutes) it waits for the next pause; if GitHub cannot be reached it asks again after 15 minutes. Nothing starts during the kill switch. Turning it on needs the second sign-in step when that is on. The "Install update" button asks once more when a conversation is going on. The live view shows a running update under "Running now" with its step and share, its outcome for an hour, and whether "overnight" is on.

head: Logs
title: Logs
text: All speech services log into their own journal (journalctl --namespace=speech-spark -u 'speech-spark-*'), capped at 500 MB and 14 days; journald deletes older entries automatically. Adjustable under Settings → Operation, effective after the next update. The panel's constant status polls are not logged at all.

head: Logs
title: Without profile names
text: Without profile names (since V01.0.443): journal lines name a profile only if it agreed under Me → Conversation → Privacy (the same switch as for Logs → Requests); otherwise they say "Profil" and the end of its id, e.g. "iphone: paired for Profil 3f2a". The admin log still names who changed something.

head: Logs
title: Diagnostic filters in the panel
text: Diagnostic filters in the panel (since V01.0.141): *Status → Logs → Diagnostic filters* replaces journalctl … | grep -E "room:|esp32:" | tail -30 on the console. Tick chat:, web search (chat: web search), homeassistant:, room:, esp32:, update and self-test (unit speech-spark-update) and errors (error, Fehler, traceback, failed, warn); several ticks mean "or", none shows every line. Time range 10 min to 24 h, 30 to 1000 lines (newest kept); "Copy" takes the output including a header with filter and hit count. Admin only, at most 60 requests per minute. Filtering runs in Python against a fixed list; only numbers from fixed lists reach journalctl. Bot tokens, bearer keys, password=/token=/key= values and logins inside URLs are blacked out before display.

head: Logs
title: Logs page "overview first"
text: Logs page "overview first" (since V01.0.212): tabs Diagnosis, Services, Update and Changes. Under Diagnosis tiles show the error count and the three busiest areas with a small history over the time range (tap to filter), below the newest error with a fixed hint (e.g. HTTP 401 from Home Assistant → token expired). Filter buttons with counts: conversation, web search, router, Home Assistant, room, speakers, Telegram, mail and "errors only". Each line shows time, area and message; errors red, warnings yellow (fixed word list in the panel), repeated lines as "×n", pauses from 2 min as a divider. Search runs in the browser over the loaded lines only. "Live" reloads every 10 s (services every 3 s) and pauses while you scroll up or select text. "Copy for thread" takes version, filter and the raw lines in a code block.

head: Logs
title: Telegram: one poller only
text: Telegram: one poller only (since V01.0.214): Telegram hands new messages to one getUpdates at a time. Up to V01.0.213 the panel's startup tasks ran twice (the https server ran them again), and the two Telegram pollers kicked each other out every 15 s ("Conflict: terminated by other getUpdates request"). Now the https server starts without its own startup tasks, and a second poller in the same process is not started. If Telegram still reports a conflict, another program uses the same bot token: the Spark then waits 5 s, 30 s, 1, 2, 5 and at most 10 min, logs only the second and every 20th time (without the token) and shows a hint under Status and Features → Telegram to use the token in one place only or get a new one from @BotFather. A single conflict right after a restart is normal (the old poll runs for up to 25 s).

head: Logs

text: Weather service briefly down (since V01.0.214): when Open-Meteo answers the weather note with 5xx or 429 or not at all, the log shows a warning ("retry in 10 min") instead of an error, and the Spark tries again every 10 min within the time window.

head: Logs
title: Web requests in the logs
text: Web requests in the logs (since V01.0.215): for web server lines ("GET /api/… 200 OK") only the status code makes a line red (500 and up), never words in the address. The panel no longer writes the log page's own requests to the journal at all. Update lines quoting a version text ("Available: 46fb0e8 …", "Update finished: …") get no colour (since V01.0.216). The time may read "+0200", "+02:00" or "Z" (since V01.0.217; before, "+02:00" left every area at 0).

head: Logs
title: Detailed diagnosis per area
text: Detailed diagnosis per area (Logs → Advanced): room mode, speakers, Home Assistant and conversation can be switched on for 15 min, 1 h or 4 h; afterwards and on every restart they are off again. They add … detail … lines with numbers and decisions only (recognition time, answer time, word count, duration of a Home Assistant call, history size, offered tools), never heard or written text, names or secrets; redaction still runs. Admin only, rate limited.

head: What gets installed
title: What gets installed
text: All services run as the system user speech. A sudoers rule lets the panel start, stop and restart the speech services and engines and trigger the update, nothing else.

head: Measuring performance
title: Measuring performance

head: Next to dgx-spark-qwen38
title: Next to dgx-spark-qwen38
text: - Ports: qwen38 uses 30000 to 30099 (engine 30000, proxy 30001, image 30020, video 30022, cockpit 30090/30091). Speech uses 31001, 31002, 31080 and 31443 (panel over https); the engines on 31011, 31012 and 31013 listen on 127.0.0.1 only. The panel rejects ports in qwen38's range, and the installer stops if a port is taken. - Memory: the GB10 has one 128 GB pool shared by CPU and GPU. The qwen38 lanes reserve a fixed share of it: 50 % with stock/fp8, 76 % in 1M mode and 85 % with flash. According to the qwen38 docs only ~16.6 GiB stay free at idle with flash, and below ~8 GiB DGX OS's earlyoom kills processes. Therefore: - If the installer detects a flash or 1M lane, it picks the 0.6B models. - Before a service loads its model it checks that the reserve stays free afterwards (default 10 GiB). If not, it does not load and the panel shows blocked with the reason. - If memory still runs short, the system kills the panel first (OOMScoreAdjust=900), then the speech services (500), not the LLM lane and not sshd (see "Speech first"). - Speech starts after the qwen38 lanes, so they take their fixed share first. - Engines start one after another, because vLLM measures free memory at start-up

head: Next to dgx-spark-qwen38
title: Next to dgx-spark-qwen38
text: and parallel starts take each other's share. - Lane switch: if you switch to flash in the cockpit, already loaded speech models stay in memory. With 1.7B models that can get too tight. Stop ASR and TTS in the panel first or switch them to 0.6B. - GPU time: ASR and TTS share the GPU with the LLM. During a transcription or speech request the LLM gets a little slower.

head: Speech first
title: Speech first
text: Speech recognition and speech output always come first (fixed rule without a switch, since V01.0.225, plan plaene/vorrang-sprache.md).

head: Speech first
title: Speech first
text: - When "speech is running": while an answer of /api/chat streams (browser, app, speakers, Telegram, Siri) and while ASR or TTS handle a request from anyone (Open WebUI and Wyoming too). The services report it through common.SpeechMark: every POST /v1/audio/... request that passed the size limit and API key touches state/speech-active. 20 seconds after that still count (follow-up question). - Background work waits during that time; its running request to the language model is cancelled (vLLM stops it when the connection closes) and repeated in the next pause, at most three times. Only one background request runs at a time. Connected: learning from conversations, memory tidy, agents, proactive notes, daily briefing, mail sorting, quality test, reading documents and meaning search (wissen.quiet()), backup (also with low CPU priority). - New hint in health.alerts: add it to live.hints too, with its place in the picture and fixed words. - New event in the audit log (guard.log): a fixed word in guard.LIVE_WORDS, then it shows under events. title: Speech first
text: round work (app/panel/vorrang.py): - r = await vorrang.post(c, "Name", url, json=..., headers=...): one request to the language model (httpx client c): waits, runs alone, is cancelled on speech and repeated; gives up with vorrang.Busy after three cancellations. - await vorrang.run("Name", lambda: coroutine()): the same for any other coroutine. - await vorrang.quiet("Name"): only wait for a pause. - await vorrang.in_thread("Name", fn, *args): CPU work (e.g. an embedding model) after a pause in its own thread with nice 15. - vorrang.hold("Name"): inside a worker thread, wait between two steps while speech runs (never call it on the event loop). - vorrang.speaking(): whether speech is running. - Operating system: the ASR and TTS services and their engines run with Nice=-5, CPUWeight=1000, IOWeight=1000. When memory runs out, the system ends the panel first (OOMScoreAdjust=900), then the speech services (500), not the LLM lane and not sshd. - GPU: the GB10 has no priorities between processes. The speech engines' memory is reserved from their start. The language model's own answer runs at the same time as the speech output and sometimes slows it down ("tts behind … inside the piece"). S

head: Priority for people
title: Priority for people
text: When several people talk at once, chosen profiles get their answer first (since V01.0.282, plan plaene/vorrang-personen.md). Off by default.

head: Priority for people
title: Priority for people
text: - Switching on: Funktionen → Gespräch → "Vorrang für Personen" (chat.person_priority, feature register vorrang). Only the admin sets the stage per profile under People and devices → profile → Rights → Priority: "Vorrang" (three profiles at most), "normal" or "hinten anstellen" (last in line). Stored in state/personen-vorrang.json (in the backup), changes in the admin log (person_priority). Under Me the profile sees the function as on or "off for you". - Who asks: only from the sign-in (browser, app, device key), never from the text. Guests and programs without a profile (Open WebUI, Wyoming) are always normal. At a shared speaker the stage counts only when the speaker recognition heard the profile's voice; the recording itself goes to the recognition as normal there, because the voice is known only afterwards. - Speech output and recognition: both services let only as many requests go to the engine at once as it takes (tts.engine_max_seqs, asr.engine_max_seqs); the rest wait in the service (common.PrioGate) by stage, then by arrival. A running request is never stopped. Every 4 s of waiting move a request one stage up, so nobody starves. At most 64 wait, else 503. A slot comes back

head: Why the installation looks like this
title: Why the installation looks like this
text: - PyTorch from the cu130 index: the aarch64 torch on PyPI has no CUDA, so a plain pip install qwen-tts would run on the CPU. torch and torchaudio must come from the same index, otherwise libtorchaudio.so does not load. - No flash-attn: there is no ARM wheel, and it reportedly does not build for sm_121. Both models use PyTorch SDPA instead. - Separate venvs for the transformers backends: qwen-asr needs transformers==4.57.6, qwen-tts transformers==4.57.3. - ASR with vLLM: vLLM 0.30 supports Qwen3-ASR natively, with /v1/audio/transcriptions, streaming and concurrent requests. It shares the environment with the TTS engine. qwen-asr[vllm] is not needed (it would force vllm 0.14). - TTS with vllm-omni: qwen-tts cannot stream. The Qwen team points to vllm-omni for streaming. vllm 0.30.0 and vllm-omni 0.30.0 have ARM wheels on PyPI (CUDA 13) and are installed natively, without Docker. - Engine memory: vLLM reserves a fixed share of the *whole* memory pool at start-up, for TTS per stage (talker and code2wav). The defaults (ASR 1.7B 0.06, 0.6B 0.035; TTS 0.04 + 0.025) are kept small so speech fits next to the qwen38 stock lane. If a share is too small, the engine stops at start-up with "No a

head: How the chat is built
title: How the chat is built
text: One answer of the assistant runs through three files in app/panel/:

head: How the chat is built
title: How the chat is built
text: - chat_turn.py (prepare): who is speaking and what they may use (profile, recognized voice, device key, Telegram, iPhone app), the system prompt, answers to waiting proposals ("yes" to an appointment, mail change, correction ...), the tools on offer and the locks after outside text. The result is a Turn with all values. - chat_tools.py (run): what a tool call does (web search, Home Assistant, mail, calendar, reminders ...). Only offered tools run; the locks are checked here again. - chat.py (_answer): asks the language model in rounds, runs tool calls through chat_tools.run, checks the answer and streams text and sound. Tool definitions and lock lists (READS_OUTSIDE, LOCKED_OUTSIDE ...) stay in chat.py.

head: How the chat is built
title: How the chat is built
text: New rights or hints go into chat_turn.py, new tools into chat_tools.py (definition and lock list in chat.py).

head: Features and rights (features.py)
title: Features and rights (features.py)
text: Since V01.0.267 every function the admin can switch is written once in app/panel/features.py: name (de/en), group, the admin switches (chat.*), the function it builds on (parent), the profile's own switch (profile), whether guests may ever use it, the Me page and the guide. Values are still stored under the old names in config.json and settings.json; only this table knows both.

head: Features and rights (features.py)
title: Features and rights (features.py)
text: - One check: features.admin_on(key), features.profile_on(key, uid), features.allowed(key, uid) and features.reason(key, uid) (reason: spark, profile, guest). Modules only ask here (admin_on, usable, allowed are one-liners); what must be set up besides (Kiwix address, agent level) the module registers in features.READY or features.GRANTED. - One list for the pages: GET /api/features (signed in, rate limited) returns every function with Spark on/off, own switch, "may" and reason; guests see only guest functions. The flags in /api/whoami and allow in /api/profile/settings and /api/iphone/settings come from the same table. - New function: an entry in features.py, a guide in guides.js. tests/test_features.py fails when a chat.* switch belongs to no function, a profile switch does not start off, or a module builds its own check. - Values in one place (since V01.0.268): common.load_config() fills every missing key from config.default.json (like jq '.[0] * .[1]' in install.sh); a second default in code (.get(k, other)) and hand merges fail the self-test. head: Keeping the live overview current (live.py)
title: Keeping the live overview current (live.py)
text: Since V01.0.312 *Status → Live* (and the monitor /live) show everything the Spark does right now. So the picture never lies by leaving something out, every change also adds its entry there:

head: Keeping the live overview current (live.py)
title: Keeping the live overview current (live.py)
text: - New tool: a target in live.TOOLS (an existing one or a new one in live.TARGETS with zone spark, lan or net) and a word in live.RETURNS. tests/test_live.py turns red when a tool from chat.py or an extra service is missing. - New kind of device: a word in live.CLIENT (the test compares with tracelog.CLIENTS). - New channel (WebSocket, long poll): a line in live._conns. - Request without a conversation (only hearing or only speaking, e.g. Wyoming): rec = live.begin(client, device), then rec.step("asr"|"tts", …) and live.end(rec, ok); refused senders with live.door(...). - Something the Spark does by itself (rule, reminder, task): live.begin(client, "", uid=…, auto=True, why="fixed word") and the steps below it inside with live.within(rec): (no way back to a device). Notes are reported by push.send itself (live.note, targets Web Push, Apple Push, Android app, Telegram); a new tag gets a word in push.WHY. - Background work runs through vorrang.run/post/in_thread/quiet/hold with a fixed name; that reports it to live.bg itself (no contents in the name). - New entry check or guard level: guard.failed and netguard.resolve already report to live.refused and live.outgoing; add new words the

head: Tests
title: Tests
text: app/tests/ holds the self-tests that run on every update (cd app && python -m unittest discover -s tests). All services are faked (tests/helpers.py); no test talks to real models or Home Assistant. tests/test_ui_browser.py also opens the panel in Chromium (Playwright) at computer and phone width: every page without script errors and without sideways scrolling, the settings search, the Me window. Without Playwright (as in the self-test on the Spark) it is skipped; on GitHub it runs in the "Tests" workflow on every push.

head: Troubleshooting
title: Troubleshooting
